subject: Mercury Health POC: prompt/log handoff and success metrics
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@mercuryhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps from today's discovery — POC inputs

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks to get the POC started:

- Goal: Verify Redwood inference reduces avg latency for our patient-facing triage flows and preserves answer accuracy on clinical Q&A.
- Success criteria we care about (initial): end-to-end median latency < 500ms for 95th pct, top-1 QA precision >= 88% on our eval set, and no PHI exfiltration risk in outputs.
- We're prepared to share ~10k anonymized prompts and the last 2 weeks of conversational logs. Need to confirm acceptable redaction levels.

Can you confirm the data formats you prefer and whether Redwood can provide a scoping template for success metrics and evaluation plan? Also please flag any compliance constraints we should know about before we hand over logs.

Attaching a short internal note that lists what we can export (will send the export bundle once format is confirmed).

Thanks,
Sasha
Director, Product
Mercury Health

Attachment: export-readme.txt (stub)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps from today's discovery — POC inputs

Hi Sasha — great to meet you and thanks for the clear goals. Quick recap from our side and a concrete plan to get the POC moving: 

Summary of proposed POC scope:
- Objective: Validate latency and QA precision on your live prompt distribution and measure cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Core success metrics: 95th pct latency < 500ms (region: US), median latency gain vs current baseline, top-1 precision on a held-out eval set >= 88% (we'll need seeded ground truth), and no high-confidence PHI-return incidents over the trial window.
- Duration: 4 weeks from data handoff (2wk initial run + 2wk guardrail monitoring).
- Ownership: Redwood (runtime + eval harness) — karthik_iyer (POC lead), Redwood CS — ben_carter (eval ops). Mercury: Sasha (product lead), Tom (security lead).

Data handoff and format (what we need):
1) CSV or NDJSON with one prompt per row and a column for context/session_id where applicable. If you have full conversation logs, NDJSON is preferred; otherwise CSV is fine.
2) A small labeled eval set (200–500 queries) with expected answers for quality measurement.
3) Indicate redaction level: we can accept PII/PHI redacted by you, or we can receive hashed identifiers — we'll sign an addendum for controlled access if raw PHI is required.

I'm attaching a PII handling checklist and a short evaluation template. For transfer: S3 or a Drive folder works. If you prefer direct S3, please share a presigned path or bucket + prefix.

Next steps I propose:
- You share sample_prompts.csv (or NDJSON) and the labeled eval.csv (due by EOD Wed 6/28)
- Redwood will run an onboarding evaluation and return a preliminary results doc and recommended config (by 7/05)
- Schedule a 30-min sync in the week of 7/08 to review findings and decide on rollout

Let me know if the timeline looks tight — we can adjust. 

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pii_handling_checklist.docx, evaluation_template.xlsx
From: Tom Whitaker <tom.w@mercuryhealth.com>

> I'm attaching a PII handling checklist and a short evaluation template. For transfer: S3 or a Drive folder works.

Thanks, Karthik — that plan looks reasonable. A few specifics from security: 

- We will provide a sample_prompts.csv (approx 1,200 rows) and a zipped chunk of NDJSON logs for the last 14 days at the S3 path below. The logs will have identifiers hashed but retain session context.
- S3 export path (internal): gs://mercury-prod-exports/prompt-logs/2028-06-01-to-2028-06-20/ (we'll provide a presigned link once legal approves).
- Redaction: we'll remove direct patient identifiers; we still expect some clinical phrases to remain. If Redwood needs raw PHI for any reason we will require an MSA addendum and a short security questionnaire.

I've attached a tiny sample prompts CSV (attached) and a short note from our security team outlining required controls. Our security contact is security@mercuryhealth.com.

Tom
Head of Platform Security
Mercury Health

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Tom. We'll take the sample_prompts.csv and the NDJSON slice and ingest into a locked staging project. A few operational notes from our side: 

- We'll run the eval harness on a canary variant first (no production keys) and run checksum audits on the input bundle.
- Ben here will coordinate the eval, produce the preliminary metrics deck, and validate latency numbers across your sample distribution.
- If you can send the presigned S3 link, we'll start the pull. If legal requires an addendum for PHI access we can pause until that's in place — please advise.

I'll own the delivery of the initial results (ETA 7/05) — karthik will share config suggestions before then.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
